content: This document is a comprehensive form designed to collect and record critical information about individuals undergoing HIV testing, diagnosis, and treatment. It includes sections for patient identification, HIV testing history, care and treatment details, maternal history (for female patients), and additional laboratory results. The form also captures data on probable routes of HIV transmission, tuberculosis status, and patient outcomes such as transfer, loss to follow-up, or death. Patient Identification The form begins with fields for recording the patient’s national identification number, clinic number, and other unique identifiers. It also includes a field for the Soundex code of the patient’s surname, which is a phonetic algorithm used for indexing names. HIV Testing and Diagnosis This section documents the types of HIV tests performed, the dates of testing, and the results. Tests include: Rapid antibody tests (initial and confirmatory) p24 antigen tests RNA polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests Proviral DNA tests HIV serological antibody tests (e.g., ELISA/EIA) HIV culture tests Western blot tests Indirect fluorescent antibody tests Recent infection testing algorithms The form also records the date and location of the patient’s most recent negative HIV test, if applicable. HIV Care and Treatment This section captures the date the patient was first enrolled in HIV care and whether they were transferred from another facility. If transferred, the name of the previous facility and the date of transfer are recorded. The form also includes: The date antiretroviral therapy (ART) was initiated The ART regimen used (first-line and second-line therapies) Whether the patient was on ART at the previous clinic The dispensing of co-trimoxazole and the date it was first provided Whether the patient is part of a discordant couple (one partner is HIV-positive, and the other is HIV-negative) Tuberculosis Status The form includes fields to document whether the patient has been diagnosed with tuberculosis (TB), the date of diagnosis, and whether TB treatment was initiated. If treatment was started, the date is also recorded. WHO Staging The form allows for the documentation of the patient’s WHO clinical stage (III or IV) and the date of diagnosis for each stage. Maternal History (For Female Patients Only) For female patients, the form asks whether the patient is currently pregnant. It also collects information about any live-born infants, including the child’s name, date of birth, and place of birth (hospital name and address). Additional Laboratory Results This section records the patient’s CD4 T-cell count and percentage, both at the time of the first test and the most recent test. It also includes the date of collection and the source of the data (laboratory or medical record). Viral load test results are also documented, including whether the viral load was detectable or undetectable, the number of copies per microliter, and the date of collection. Probable Route of Transmission The form provides checkboxes to indicate the likely mode of HIV transmission, including: Sexual contact with males or females Injection drug use Blood transfusion or organ transplant Heterosexual contact with specific risk factors (e.g., with an HIV-infected person, a person who injects drugs, a bisexual male, or a sex worker) Transfer Out and Death This section records the date of transfer to another facility, the name and location of the facility, and the date of loss to follow-up or death. If the patient has died, the cause of death (HIV-related or non-HIV-related) and the place of death are documented. Ministry of Health Use The final section is reserved for use by the Ministry of Health. It includes fields for the date the form was received, the type of report (new case or follow-up), and any additional comments. Countries are encouraged to adapt the form to include specific demographic characteristics, transmission risk categories, and facility types as needed. This form is a critical tool for person-centered HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance, ensuring that comprehensive and standardized data is collected to guide patient care and public health interventions.
